_comment: English bodies for langchain (framework). Mechanism per C0-1..6. No extraSections in source; sections/sectionTitles omitted. layer_position/providers not rendered — not included.

axes.model_access: The model-access layer is its home-turf capability: a unified interface family across LLMs/embeddings/tools (the provider integration surface is huge, per the official integrations catalog, not itemized one by one); it does not call models itself — it is the abstraction layer where "switch providers without changing code".
axes.runtime: Python/JS libraries (pip/npm installed into your process); GitHub 148,205★ (API verified 2026-10-21) — the main body of the LLM application framework ecosystem. The companion LangGraph (orchestration) / LangSmith (observability) are adjacent product lines from the same vendor.
axes.local_files: Library form running inside your own code and process; where data lands is decided by your integrations (vector stores/files all on your side).
axes.background: The library itself has no resident semantics; residency depends on the application you build with it. The official hosted line (the LangSmith platform) is a separate product surface.
axes.tools: Tool definition and invocation abstractions are a core surface; an MCP adapter line exists (langchain-mcp-adapters), support details not itemized.
axes.context: The memory/retrieval component family (buffer/window/entity etc.) is its traditional narrative; cross-session memory requires wiring your own storage — the components give the pattern, not hosting.
axes.permissions: No account system (library form); the permissions surface = the various vendors' API keys and tool capabilities you wire in. The observability line (LangSmith) has a data-upload surface — default behavior not itemized.
axes.fit: Fits: wanting the largest integration ecosystem, wanting an abstraction layer where "switch providers without changing code", starting out with RAG/tool flows. Does not fit: lightweight direct calls to a single vendor's API (the abstraction layer is a cost); wanting a batteries-included agent runtime (that is the LangGraph/Deep Agents line).

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/framework/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/framework/_protocol.md).
unknowns:
- The full integrations catalog and official-maintenance markers (not itemized one by one)
- The current capability surface of the MCP adapter (not itemized)
- Details of LangSmith's default data-upload behavior (not itemized)
related: Same-vendor orchestration line: LangChain gives components, LangGraph gives the graph and runtime.
Same-vendor batteries-included line: when you don't want to hand-build the whole loop, use its deep-agent skeleton.
